For this thread, we will discuss automation and its relation to the upcoming "fourth industrial revolution".

[Machine learning](http://www.computerworld.com/article/2935628/data-mining/ibm-prepares-spark-for-machine-learning.html) is a development every heavyweight technology firm is taking seriously; in terms of resource investment, it's put on the same level as [abandoning silicon](http://arstechnica.com/gadgets/2015/02/intel-forges-ahead-to-10nm-will-move-away-from-silicon-at-7nm/) for processors. The direction markets are moving towards has already been called the upcoming fourth industrial revolution, and is projected to cost-effectively eradicate many task-oriented office jobs. Though previously hindered by limitations in hardware, [that may no longer be an issue.](http://newsroom.intel.com/community/intel_newsroom/blog/2015/07/28/intel-and-micron-produce-breakthrough-memory-technology)

Will machines replace humans in sedentary careers? Will all jobs below decision-makers disappear? How long will it take? *Why* do firms chase productive capital investment when humans are capable of the same tasks?

Discuss.
